newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia net share investment seen $10 bln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Russia net share investment seen $10 bln by 2000.

text.p: Net annual investment in Russian shares could soar to $10-11 billion in 2000 from just $1 billion last year, a securities market official said on Wednesday.
Dmitry Subbotin, head of the resource secretariat at the Federal Commission for the Securities Market, said this was a target figure but that it was realistically attainable.
He said turnover in the share market, of $5 billion in 1995, could rise to $30-80 billion by the end of the century.
Market capitalisation could rise to $80-130 billion from $20 billion, he told a conference.
Subbotin said the figures were based on information from investors, market intermediaries and on comparison with what had happened in other countries.
"It sounds realistic and we believe we know the bottlenecks which need to be sorted out," he said.
Andrei Volgin, director of Adamant Financial Corporation and chairman of the Moscow Shareholders' Rights Committee, said the target was realistic.
He told the conference that stock prices could rise a further 20-50 percent on average by the end of the year.

He said an end to concern over the health of President Boris Yeltsin, who is due to have heart surgery soon, the entry of Russia into an International Finance Corporation index of emerging markets and a rating for Russian debt could all help stock prices.
"Russian debt is already up significantly and many investors in Russian debt are likely to swap from debt to equities as they believe they are undervalued."
Volgin said stocks were likely to move in line with Russian economic recovery but that investors could also benefit by seeking to restructure companies.
Western investors have in the past been put off by infrastructural problems such as settlement and doubts over share registries.
Subbotin said the question of settlement was being discussed. He believed any system should be market-based and owned by the institutions it served.
